quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you do to avoid confusing other drivers?

options.text: Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
Use your horn only in emergency situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal after you finish turning or changing lanes. Leaving it on confuses other drivers about which direction you are going.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that the road will be divided ahead.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should maintain in good conditions?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance when conditions are poor.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Provide you with an escape route.
Communicate your intentions to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you receive wind blasts.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should help you avoid wind blasts, not receive them. A good position helps you see others, be seen, avoid hazards, and gives you an escape route. It also shows other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, what should a motorcycle rider NOT do?

options.text: Choose a lane position that increases their visibility.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Cover the clutch and brakes to reduce their reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach an intersection. Choose a position where other drivers can see you. Ready your clutch and brakes. Do not speed up or make sudden moves, as this confuses other drivers.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: You believe stopping will be routine.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement is slippery.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when the road is slippery, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy. Your motorcycle needs more distance to stop safely.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: Doesn't mean that they will properly yield to you.
Guarantees that they will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doesn't mean that they will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that eye contact means another driver will yield to you. Many drivers look directly at motorcycles but still do not see them.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of other vehicles to see ahead. Stay flexible with your lane position.

questions.question: If you must shift gears while in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
Is better than shifting before the curve.
Is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden power change can cause your rear wheel to skid.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
In a position that allows you to most effectively see and be seen.
In the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a position that allows you to most effectively see and be seen.
questions.explanation: Position your motorcycle to see ahead and be seen by others. For a left curve, stay on the right side to see oncoming traffic. For a right curve, stay left-center so you can see ahead safely without getting too close to oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: When someone passes you on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the middle of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed on your left, stay in the middle of your lane. Riding on the right side can be dangerous. It may encourage the other driver to move back into your lane too quickly.

questions.question: How does your steering feel if your front tire goes flat?
questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy.
questions.explanation: Heavy steering is a sign that your front tire may be flat. Stop and check your tires as soon as possible.

questions.question: Which action does NOT help you stay in control while turning on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up while turning.
questions.explanation: To stay in control while turning, slow down before you enter the turn. Look where you want to go. Lean into the turn by pressing on the handlebar. Gently speed up as you go through the turn to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: What is the best position to ride in within a lane?

options.text: There is no single best position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position.
questions.explanation: There is no single best position in a lane. A good rider changes their position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: How should you brake when making a normal stop on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use the front and rear brakes together at the same time. Also downshift.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on the back of slow-moving vehicles. These vehicles move slower than 25 mph, such as farm equipment, construction machinery, or horse-drawn carts.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.
The rear brake is stronger than the front brake.
Both brakes have equal stopping power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Riding on ______ can give you poor grip on the road.
questions.correctAnswerText: Pavement markings
questions.explanation: You may have poor grip on wet pavement, snow, ice, mud, gravel, lane markings, steel plates, and utility hole covers.

questions.question: When being passed, moving to the far side of your lane:

options.text: Is a good idea because you will be farther from the other vehicle.
Is not a good idea because it may cause the other driver to return to your lane too soon.
Does not matter because it has no effect on safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not a good idea because it may cause the other driver to return to your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far side of your lane when being passed. This may encourage the other driver to move back into your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: Is eye protection required for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders must use proper eye protection when riding in Georgia.

questions.question: If you carry a passenger on your motorcycle, what must you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You need to add air pressure to your tires before riding. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist change gears before starting a turn?

options.text: To avoid a sudden change in power during the turn.
To keep both hands on the handle grips during the turn.
To keep the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid a sudden change in power during the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you turn. Shifting while turning can cause the rear wheel to suddenly change power and skid. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly to prevent skidding.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then do the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then do the other.
questions.explanation: Do braking and swerving as separate actions. Never brake while swerving because this can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Stop completely, then go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane is ending.
